name: Ford - Sterling Axle Plant, Sterling Heights MI

fieldNotes.site: Ford Sterling Axle Plant, 39000 Mound Rd, Sterling Heights (Macomb County) MI - an active Ford components plant operating since 1956, ~2,295 employees, producing rear axles for the F-150, Super Duty, Expedition, Navigator, Mustang and Transit. LOCATION CORRECTION: the roster address (29900 Mound Rd) and geocode (42.5141,-83.0466, RANGE_INTERPOLATED) are WRONG - they point at an office/tech campus ~3.5 km south. Correct address is 39000 Mound Rd, Sterling Heights MI 48310 (confirmed via Ford Authority, Waze, CommercialCafe). Exact coordinates 42.583580,-83.044966 obtained from the US EPA Superfund site profile for the Ford Motor Company Sterling Axle Plant - confirmed by satellite as the large multi-roof Ford plant building bounded by Mound Rd on the west.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Confirmed - Street View (2025) on Mound Rd at the NW corner shows a wide gated truck entrance: a tractor pulling an intermodal container is seen exiting through a chain-link sliding-gate opening, with trailers parked inside the yard and dock doors on the adjacent building face. Chain-link perimeter fencing runs the full Mound Rd frontage. truckGateCount 1 (primary truck gate at the NW).
fieldNotes.guardShack: Marked true at medium confidence - a fenced ~2,295-employee active Ford plant of this scale conventionally operates a staffed gatehouse. A small structure is visible beside the NW truck gate but a clear guard-booth could not be positively confirmed - the gate may be badge/remote-controlled. Flagged uncertain along with remoteGs.
fieldNotes.preGateStaging: Marked false (uncertain) - the NW truck gate opens more or less directly into the drop yard / dock area; no clear dedicated pre-gate truck staging apron outside the gate identified. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: True - the internal yard between the NW gate and the dock doors provides post-gate queue/holding room.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: True - the internal yard from the NW truck gate to the dock doors and through the drop yard is deep, with room to queue 3+ trucks.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Estimated 10-25 dock doors along the NE/E building faces serving the drop yard; exact count obscured by roof angle - flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropArea: NW/N drop yard holds an estimated 15-20 parked trailers in rows amid material laydown areas (z19 imagery); banded 10-25. dropYard true. trailersVisible ~18.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Marked false (medium confidence) - freight is concentrated on the N/NE side; no clearly separate second dock cluster confirmed. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail spur runs into the property from the rail yard on the east, serving the N/NE material laydown area - rail-served.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: False - a single large interconnected plant building (multi-roof but one structure); buildingCount 1.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Sterling Heights is a dense Detroit-metro suburb; the plant is hemmed by continuous suburban/industrial development - Urban.
